question: Does the 75-125 kpc Gaussian extent preferred by P0568 correspond to the measured spatial extent of registered stars plus hot gas rather than a new gravity-routing length?

components.members: spectroscopic/photometric member-light catalog used by the raw-lens program
components.accept_gas_spherical: absolute line-of-sight projection of measured ACCEPT electron-density shells
components.accept_gas_sqrt_morphology: same absolute radial gas mass modulated by square-root Chandra morphology with annular mass preserved
components.accept_gas_linear_morphology: same absolute radial gas mass modulated linearly by Chandra morphology with annular mass preserved
components.stars_plus_gas: absolute ACCEPT gas plus HST light normalized to published Tian BCG stellar mass
components.tian_anchor_sensitivity: ACCEPT gas rescaled to the incompatible Tian central spherical gas anchor

extent_metrics.primary_component: accept_absolute stars_plus_gas with square-root Chandra morphology

interpretation_gates.extent_match: median primary sigma equivalent lies inside 75-125 kpc
interpretation_gates.system_coverage: at least three of four primary systems lie inside the band under either RMS- or R80-equivalent sigma
interpretation_gates.meaning: Passing makes missing measured baryonic extent a sufficient scale explanation; it does not prove the map has the correct lensing amplitude or angular structure.

claim_limits: The stellar map has one global BCG mass normalization and no resolved mass-to-light model for satellites or intracluster light.
ACCEPT publishes diagonal electron-density errors but not full shell covariance.
The registered map is limited to 120 arcsec across, truncating very extended gas.
The four systems and component constructions are spent; this is a scale audit, not validation.
Matching an extent does not establish a new field equation or reproduce raw lensing.
